title: Shortening a bounded finite-presentation flat affine complex by residue vanishing
statement: Let S be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and B a cochain complex of O_S-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] concentrated in [0,b], for b∈ℕ. Assume every term is flat over id_S, quasi-coherent, and finitely presented. Let d∈ℕ. Suppose for every s∈S and q∈ℕ with d<q, the homology H^q((fromSpecResidueField s)*B) is zero. Then there is D on the same S concentrated in [0,d], termwise flat and quasi-coherent, whose global-section ring complex is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and H^q(g*D)≅H^q(g*B) for every scheme morphism g:T′→S and q∈ℕ [def-pc-base-change].

source.place: Tags 068V (residue criterion, specialized to bounded projective complexes), 064U (finite free representatives), 08EB (affine model)

proof.text: Identify S with Spec A. Affine quasi-coherent sheaves are modules, and evaluation is exact on this subcategory. The section terms of B are finitely presented flat A-modules, hence finite projective. The section complex P is concentrated in [0,b], and its associated-sheaf complex recovers B and its differentials. Ordinary residue pullback is tensor with κ(p).

Run descending induction on the top degree m>d of P. Fibre homology at m is coker(d^{m-1}⊗κ(p)). This is zero for every prime by the hypothesis. The finite cokernel of d^{m-1} therefore has zero localization at every prime by local Nakayama and is zero. Thus d^{m-1} is surjective and splits since P^m is projective. Decompose P^{m-1}=ker(d^{m-1})⊕P^m; the kernel is finite projective. The complex relation forces the preceding differential into the kernel. The two copies of P^m give an identity-differential contractible summand, so cancelling it gives a chain homotopy equivalence to a complex with lower top degree. Repeat until the top is at most d. This is the bounded-projective special case of the residue criterion 068V, with its cancellation argument written explicitly. Nonnegative support is preserved because m>d≥0 implies m-1≥0. If b≤d no cancellation is required.

Associate sheaves to the shortened finite-projective complex. Its terms are flat and quasi-coherent. It is pseudo-coherent in the ring definition: choose finite-projective complements in finite free modules, add the complements as identity-differential contractible pairs, and descend from the highest degree. This constructs a bounded-above finite free complex with the same derived image; it may continue indefinitely to the left, which the definition allows. This is the finite-projective-to-finite-free part of Tag 064U.

Each chain homotopy equivalence obtained by cancelling a contractible pair is preserved by tensor and by ordinary sheaf pullback. Take homology after arbitrary g:T′→S to obtain the asserted comparisons, with no affineness assumption on T′. All steps kept S fixed. The zero-ring case uses the zero complex; at d=0 the resulting representative is a finite projective module in degree zero.
